{"new_lineages":[{"id":"L-code-is-data","scope":"language","statement":"Code is data, erasing the distinction between code and data, following the Lisp model."},{"id":"L-type-carries-its-laws","scope":"language","statement":"A type (or function) carries, as a proposition, the law its values must satisfy."},{"id":"L-identifiers-central","scope":"language","statement":"Identifiers are central: a simple label recovers a complex object, the dictionary joining human and machine."},{"id":"L-remaking-foundations","scope":"other","statement":"He has re-made the language many times, each time rethinking the foundations of programming more deeply."},{"id":"L-states-as-type-algebra","scope":"language","statement":"States and channels and their multiplicities are represented with type algebra (sum for states, product for channels), with a constructor from a number to a set."},{"id":"L-semantic-then-efficient","scope":"language","statement":"Once semantic validity and equivalence are established, a clear slow algorithm can be replaced by an efficient equivalent one, enabling optimization."},{"id":"L-code-to-understand","scope":"other","statement":"He codes to understand, which means being able to manipulate the code and see how changes affect its observables."},{"id":"L-dependent-types-def","scope":"language","statement":"Dependent types are types that depend on a value, taking the cardinality of that value's type."},{"id":"L-express-extracomputational","scope":"language","statement":"The language expresses extra-computational concepts like probability by abstracting their properties and verifying compliance (e.g. a probability lies in [0,1])."},{"id":"L-expressiveness","scope":"language","statement":"Code must express its intention to both the human reader and the compiler, referring truthfully to known structures."},{"id":"L-create-objects-uniformly","scope":"language","statement":"The language expresses and creates values, variables, types and functions uniformly, with their semantics."},{"id":"L-reasoning-to-code-isomorphism","scope":"language","statement":"There should be a one-to-one relation between reasoning and the flow of the code, so running the code verifies the reasoning."},{"id":"L-primitives","scope":"language","statement":"A proposed set of primitive value types and primitive functions."},{"id":"L-sample-probability-duality","scope":"language","statement":"Sample and probability form a duality, with tests demonstrating it holds."},{"id":"L-semantics-own-universe","scope":"language","statement":"The semantics lives in its own universe, not that of C++, even while using C++ structures to express it."},{"id":"L-foundation-choice","scope":"language","statement":"Open question of which foundation to build on (type theory vs category theory, HoTT vs ZMT)."},{"id":"L-environment-stores-retrieves","scope":"language","statement":"The environment is a map of definitions whose two mechanisms are storing and retrieving variables by name."},{"id":"L-environment-resources","scope":"language","statement":"The environment needs and manages resources (memory and compute) and function execution, a problem that ties to it but exceeds it (OS, compiler)."},{"id":"L-environment-first-object","scope":"language","statement":"The environment is the first object the language must define, since data is loaded into it."},{"id":"L-environment-kinds","scope":"language","statement":"There are simple environments (one value type, one identifier) and compound ones that admit multiple."},{"id":"L-variable-is-fields","scope":"language","statement":"A variable is a name, a memory address, a size and a type; the type contains the size and the name can be the address."},{"id":"L-variable-not-know-environment","scope":"language","statement":"A variable knows its name but should not know its environment, so its resource acquisition stays predictable."},{"id":"L-constructors-in-type-space","scope":"language","statement":"Constructors should live in each type's space rather than in the global space."},{"id":"L-types-make-code-safe","scope":"language","statement":"Declaring a function declares the tests it must pass, so types encode preconditions and gate membership on testing, yielding self-verified programs."},{"id":"L-type-definition-recursive","scope":"language","statement":"A type's definition is necessarily recursive, since the type must be universally accessible like identifiers."},{"id":"L-constructor-vs-function","scope":"language","statement":"A constructor differs from a function in that a constructor plus its parameters is the element, making elements transparent, while a function involves a computation."},{"id":"L-two-kinds-of-definition","scope":"language","statement":"There are two ways to define types, the constructive and the declarative."},{"id":"L-function-holds-code","scope":"language","statement":"A function holds its code written in the language plus a compiled simplified form."},{"id":"L-code-operations","scope":"language","statement":"The language builds in functions that operate on code: tests, errors, derivatives, finding equivalents, and timing."},{"id":"L-dynamic-naming","scope":"language","statement":"For dynamically created types or functions, a name is really an address, so a generated numeric identifier suffices."},{"id":"L-language-self-writing","scope":"language","statement":"Defining new types and functions should itself be programmable, the language writing itself, which requires a simple robust language with no syntactic sugar."},{"id":"L-identifier-type-independent","scope":"language","statement":"The identifier and the type are completely independent; the identifier is a fantasy name unknown until resolved."},{"id":"L-subtype-by-predicate","scope":"language","statement":"A subtype (subObject) is the subset of a type whose values satisfy a predicate, a test."},{"id":"L-element-belongs-one-type","scope":"language","statement":"Each element belongs to exactly one type but can serve to build many types."},{"id":"L-inject-multiple-identifiers","scope":"language","statement":"A type or function can inject more than one identifier into the environment."},{"id":"L-composition-dot","scope":"language","statement":"Composition is written with a dot, which explains class methods."},{"id":"L-equals-assertion","scope":"language","statement":"The equals sign is an assertion that both sides are equal, also used for pattern matching when a symbol is unknown."},{"id":"L-test-result-one-or-explanation","scope":"language","statement":"A check returns success (one) if met or an explanation of why it failed, not just a boolean."},{"id":"L-function-kinds","scope":"language","statement":"Functions are of two kinds: predefined and user defined."},{"id":"L-type-autodetection","scope":"language","statement":"Types can be handled by autodetection."},{"id":"L-sum-types-with-bar","scope":"language","statement":"Types are expressed as alternatives with a bar, as in maybe, either and sum."},{"id":"L-function-type-expression","scope":"language","statement":"Open question of how to express the type of a function such as write : a -> string."},{"id":"L-learn-from-each-run","scope":"language","statement":"From each run of the code something is learned, whether an implementation is correct or how fast it is."},{"id":"L-simultaneous-definition","scope":"language","statement":"When postconditions are interdependent, objects are defined together, in tuples with crossconditions, the one form of definition."},{"id":"L-pre-postconditions","scope":"language","statement":"Functions and types are defined by preconditions and postconditions, the postconditions defining the subtype."},{"id":"L-language-parts-compiler","scope":"language","statement":"The language has parts: a grammar with semantic rules and a front compiler to C++."},{"id":"L-express-math-structures","scope":"language","statement":"The language must express mathematical structures (category, functor, group) with their laws, possibly in several declaration dependent types."},{"id":"L-couplings-as-types","scope":"language","statement":"Energetic couplings, binding schemes and conformational spaces are represented and certified as types."},{"id":"L-hott-prob-tension","scope":"language","statement":"There is a tension between HoTT's invertible identities and univalence and probability's non-invertible uncertainty, with no fully unified model yet."},{"id":"L-hott-ingredients-sufficient","scope":"language","statement":"Sigma-types, Pi-types, identity types and HITs suffice to encode conformational models, energetic couplings and symmetry structures."},{"id":"L-types-spaces-identities-paths","scope":"language","statement":"HoTT gives types as spaces and identities as paths, its internal equality replacing ad hoc isomorphisms."},{"id":"L-likelihood-type-propagation","scope":"other","statement":"Likelihood recursion is encoded via type-theoretic propagation, with noise structures and model boundaries as dependent types."},{"id":"L-markov-generated","scope":"language","statement":"Markov models become generated objects rather than arbitrary inputs."},{"id":"L-dsl-as-model-compiler","scope":"language","statement":"The DSLs are model compilers that translate high-level mechanistic specifications into executable, inferable structures."},{"id":"L-meta-layer","scope":"language","statement":"The language sits as a meta-layer above the ConformationalModel DSL, MacroIR and Bayesian pipelines."},{"id":"L-embedded-semantic-structure","scope":"language","statement":"Biological models carry embedded semantic structure such as symmetry groups, compositional operators and equivalence classes."},{"id":"L-proof-assistants-verify","scope":"language","statement":"Proof assistants (Coq, Lean, Agda) can verify the semantic correctness of biological models via type-checking."},{"id":"L-separate-structure-inference","scope":"language","statement":"Deterministic structural validity (via HoTT) is kept separate from probabilistic inference (via Bayesian layers), probability handled downstream."},{"id":"L-symmetry-as-identity-paths","scope":"language","statement":"Symmetry reductions are path-based identities that collapse state redundancies into reduced Markov spaces."},{"id":"L-sampler-type-indexed","scope":"other","statement":"Sampler state spaces and parameter manifolds are treated as type-indexed temperature-ladder manifolds."},{"id":"L-compile-time-prevents-invalid","scope":"language","statement":"The type system prevents invalid models from being constructed, eliminating consistency violations at compile time before execution or inference."},{"id":"L-type-safe-priors","scope":"other","statement":"Type-safe prior spaces bridge the MacroIR likelihood engine with structural model spaces."},{"id":"L-formalize-state-energy-algebra","scope":"language","statement":"Planned work to formalize a type system for state and energy algebra and HoTT-based state composition primitives."},{"id":"L-models-as-well-typed-objects","scope":"language","statement":"Biological models are well-typed objects where types are molecular states, identity paths are symmetries, and composition emerges from dependent type operations."},{"id":"L-dsl-unifies-domains","scope":"language","statement":"One DSL framework unifies models across channels, enzymes, networks, signaling and regulation."},{"id":"L-identity-paths-equivalences","scope":"language","statement":"Identity paths represent structural equivalences between model entities."},{"id":"L-encode-as-types","scope":"language","statement":"Model components, entities and deterministic structure are encoded as types."},{"id":"L-hottification-definition","scope":"language","statement":"HoTTification is transforming a scientific model, algorithm or modeling language into a formal structure governed by HoTT, analogous to categorification or quantization."},{"id":"L-hottification-models-typed-objects","scope":"language","statement":"Under HoTTification models themselves become typed mathematical objects whose equivalences, symmetries and compositions are validated by the type system."},{"id":"L-machine-verifiable-theories","scope":"other","statement":"HoTTification offers a path toward machine-verifiable biological theories."},{"id":"L-runtime-vs-semantic-safety","scope":"language","statement":"Runtime safety prevents crashes while semantic safety, a layer above runtime, prevents invalid models from existing at all."},{"id":"L-dep-types-semantic-safety","scope":"language","statement":"Dependent typing enforces semantic safety, guaranteeing the internal consistency of model compositions."},{"id":"L-higher-paths-symmetries","scope":"language","statement":"Higher-order symmetries and transformations between equivalences are captured as higher paths."},{"id":"L-bayesian-mapping","scope":"other","statement":"Scientific knowledge production is mapped into explicit Bayesian structures (introduction to prior, methods to likelihood, results to observations, discussion to posterior) to make reasoning auditable and probabilistic."},{"id":"L-compositional-kinetic","scope":"language","statement":"Kinetic models are built compositionally from conformational state components as an external product of degrees of freedom with energetic coupling rules and state aggregation."},{"id":"L-fisher-validation","scope":"other","statement":"A likelihood implementation is validated by agreement between the Fisher Information Matrix from score covariance and the one from the Hessian, without full inference."},{"id":"L-macroir-consumes-models","scope":"other","statement":"MacroIR consumes structurally defined Markov models and computes interval-averaged likelihoods for macroscopic current data."}],

models."},{"id":"L-adjoint-forward-diagnostic","scope":"language","statement":"Each forward operation (simulate, infer) is paired by adjunction with a diagnostic approximation (recover, arbitrary unit tests."},{"id":"L-tests-as-morphisms","scope":"language","statement":"Each CLI operation is a typed morphism and each test a witness path or triangle identity, not a patch."},{"id":"L-epistemic-firewall","scope":"language","statement":"The SAV verification layer acts as an epistemic firewall defending the system against silent semantic drift during refactoring."},{"id":"L-pre-formal-safety","scope":"language","statement":"Semantic contracts and diagnostics form a pre-formal, soft homotopy layer that structures and defends correctness before hard groupoid structure."},{"id":"L-epistemic-compression","scope":"language","statement":"A few adjunction-derived tests cover most of the risk; verification is compressed into a minimal, epistemically meaningful suite."},{"id":"L-contagiously-safe-dsl","scope":"language","statement":"A compile-time safe model DSL whose safety is contagious, propagating through the system via the compiler, with regions."},{"id":"L-semantic-zones-kernel","scope":"language","statement":"A type-theoretic HoTT kernel provides a formal model/inference algebra plus constructible semantic zones for than syntactic and type safety arising from epistemic clarity."},{"id":"L-hottification-roadmap","scope":"method","statement":"HoTTification is a staged program, a semantic elevation not a rewrite, paths."},{"id":"L-declarative-and-optimizer","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier is at once a declarative language and an optimization tool: you declare what you want and it openly shuffles {"new_lineages":[{"id":"L-path-equivalence-fundamental","scope":"language","statement":"Path equivalence is Luthier's fundamental concept, and proving different implementations equivalent is the hardest core of the design."},{"id":"L-core-plus-libraries","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier is a closed core plus libraries, the libraries being the functions that connect it to what is external (C++, Python, the machine), modeled as a kind of external element."},{"id":"L-closed-observer","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier is a closed, complete universe that observes the outside world and communicates with it through a read/write that is also a compilation/reading."},{"id":"L-abstraction-to-express-ideas","scope":"language","statement":"The most interesting role of Luthier is as a relator, an abstraction mechanism to express ideas like probability, sample, matrix, units and experiment."},{"id":"L-decorator-algebra","scope":"language","statement":"Decorator composition has algebraic properties (associativity, commutativity) that should be expressible and used to represent it in the simplest form."},{"id":"L-decorators-error","scope":"language","statement":"Decorators express the error of a number and its propagation (derivatives), previously done in C++ with templates, now expressible easily."},{"id":"L-start-from-reals","scope":"language","statement":"Start from the ABC: reals, their operations, and a concept of error of the reals."},{"id":"L-express-invariances","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier's aim is to express the invariances of the disciplines (a species mates within itself, electrons are fermions, photons bosons)."},{"id":"L-function-by-properties","scope":"language","statement":"A function is defined from its properties, the propositions its inputs and outputs satisfy, not only operationally, keeping both."},{"id":"L-implementation-of-concept","scope":"language","statement":"A definition in Luthier should uniquely determine that something is an implementation of a concept, e.g. of matrices."},{"id":"L-non-univocal-functions","scope":"language","statement":"The language itself lets one model non-univocal functions, functions with error, samples, from the start."},{"id":"L-conceptual-first","scope":"method","statement":"The first step is to think the concepts with depth; translation and implementation come later even if hard."},{"id":"L-statements-commute","scope":"language","statement":"Statements in a Luthier program commute, their order not changing the result, with temporality reconstructed from type dependency rather than textual order."},{"id":"L-program-not-a-type","scope":"language","statement":"HoTT models each statement but not the program as a whole, a series of statements/types; it has no concept of a complete program, a theoretical limbo."},{"id":"L-program-is-element-meta","scope":"language","statement":"A Luthier program is itself an element of Luthier, operable by Luthier; meta-recursion is native from the start, the code being the first element, not a later graft as in Lisp."},{"id":"L-first-class-contexts","scope":"language","statement":"The context should be treated as a type in itself, first-class contexts, to lift the program out of the limbo."},{"id":"L-context-as-dag","scope":"language","statement":"The context or program is modeled as a Directed Acyclic Graph of definitions where types depend on other types."},{"id":"L-expressivity-over-redundancy","scope":"language","statement":"Expressivity is preferred over forced redundancy, with good compiler messages supplying robustness, since redundancy can be uncomfortable and limit needlessly."},{"id":"L-no-double-definition","scope":"language","statement":"The compiler verifies no type is defined twice, or a double definition is read as a Cartesian product running two ways."},{"id":"L-forward-undefined-types","scope":"language","statement":"One may refer to types not yet defined and define them later, or leave them undefined, in which case they act as program inputs."},{"id":"L-implicit-types","scope":"language","statement":"Types can be defined implicitly as solutions to a problem or as the optimum of a function, rather than declared directly."},{"id":"L-forgetting-problem","scope":"language","statement":"Composing dependent functions accumulates a growing typing load where the decoration can dwarf the value, the forgetting problem, one of Luthier's fundamental problems."},{"id":"L-simplify-dependent-composition","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier needs a simplifying typing algebra, not a free monoid, to keep the resulting type's complexity bounded when composing dependent types, a key engineering problem."},{"id":"L-truncation-operators","scope":"language","statement":"Crude truncation or arbitrary forgetting to clean a complex type is rejected: with dependent types you must have a well-defined algebra of dependent types."},{"id":"L-type-holds-history","scope":"language","statement":"What a type holds is the history of how you arrived at it."},{"id":"L-forgetful-functors-key","scope":"language","statement":"Which forgetting function (a non-invertible selective-forgetting function) you apply to types defines the language you speak, making forgetful functors one of Luthier's most important components."},{"id":"L-associativity-patterns","scope":"language","statement":"If functions are associative, patterns in composition can be exploited, e.g. a loop is a series of functions to a power, keeping the type expressed with an exponent."},{"id":"L-forgetting-functions-optimize-different","scope":"language","statement":"Different forgetting functions optimize different things (compute, compilation, precision), so understanding their properties and which to use for what is fundamental."},{"id":"L-commuting-squares","scope":"language","statement":"Coherence of forgetting and function application is analyzed with commuting squares: forget-then-apply must equal apply-then-forget, the two paths compared for equivalence."},{"id":"L-express-alternatives","scope":"language","statement":"The point is not to do everything but to have the tools to express different alternatives, none best or worst, even to convince yourself something is useless."},{"id":"L-optimize-own-rules","scope":"language","statement":"Since he invents the language, its rules can be optimized to make working on and manipulating Luthier programs easy."},{"id":"L-combine-dags","scope":"language","statement":"Operating on Luthier is combining DAGs of definitions, where the concept of substitution (as in defining a function) comes into play."},{"id":"L-time-as-dependency","scope":"language","statement":"Time, the order of things, is modeled mathematically as dependency between definitions: one thing depending on another gives a time."},{"id":"L-defpath-bayesian","scope":"language","statement":"A path between two implementations is declared with a defPath whose proof is a Bayesian estimate, Path being logical proof plus Bayesian evidence."},{"id":"L-delegation-easy","scope":"language","statement":"Delegation should be easy, an idea traced to Modelica, a specification of a program without implementation."},{"id":"L-description-language","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier's first stage is a language for describing the problem, the functions and the conditions under which they work, the emphasis on explicitation rather than execution."},{"id":"L-execution-is-verifying-equivalences","scope":"language","statement":"As mathematics does not execute but only verifies equivalences, execution in Luthier is that verification of equivalences."},{"id":"L-levels-of-equivalence","scope":"language","statement":"A fundamental idea of Luthier is to express different levels of equivalence (same information, isomorphic, exactly equal, same memory location), each a different equivalence functor."},{"id":"L-equivalence-essential-vs-decoration","scope":"language","statement":"Function equivalences separate what is essential (the equivalent) from what is decoration (efficiency, cost), the non-equivalent."},{"id":"L-core-few-primitives","scope":"language","statement":"There is a clear core of Luthier where all its operations execute, with only a few primitives implemented in C or similar so it runs."},{"id":"L-probabilities-types-together","scope":"language","statement":"Probabilities and types go almost together so the equivalences themselves are probabilistic, with HoTT giving the universe of points where the probabilities apply."},{"id":"L-minimalism-founding-components","scope":"language","statement":"The minimalism is in the founding components, from which a huge edifice of complex concepts is built, reducing everything to few minimal elements without resigning expressivity."},{"id":"L-category-theory-style-definitions","scope":"language","statement":"Basic elements are defined category-theory style, functors defined from arrows, from basal elements."},{"id":"L-dependent-types-basic","scope":"language","statement":"Dependent types are probably one of the basic initial concepts of the language."},{"id":"L-compile-to-targets","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier describes functions and equivalences and maps them to other languages (C, C++, Java), not directly but by giving the facilities so others can extend the translation."},{"id":"L-dont-execute-until-defined","scope":"language","statement":"Code is not executed until it is fully defined, so undefined dead code can sit harmlessly without bothering anyone."},{"id":"L-function-vs-interactive","scope":"language","statement":"A Luthier program is modeled first as a pure function (input to output) for simplicity, extendable later to an interactive model."},{"id":"L-code-many-operations","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier code is an object you can do many operations on, verify, compile, run, not just compile and run, trading complexity for expressivity."}],

{"new_lineages":[{"id":"L-hot-values-paths","scope":"language","statement":"Hot values open a larger universe of possible paths than ordinary values."},{"id":"L-particle-filtering-paths","scope":"language","statement":"The exponential explosion of the path space is handled by particle filtering: running several stochastic programs in design."},{"id":"L-express-then-execute","scope":"language","statement":"You first express the ideas with pencil and paper and then go to execution or the empirical database; these are two layers, not opposed philosophies."},{"id":"L-quantifiers-first-class","scope":"language","statement":"The logical quantifiers for-all and exists should be first-class citizens of things."},{"id":"L-living-vs-dead-language","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier can be a living language that acts or a dead language that only describes; the descriptive role is where it starts."},{"id":"L-syntax-semantics-before-implementation","scope":"method","statement":"Fix Luthier's syntax and semantics on paper first, and only then implement structure."},{"id":"L-generic-concept-contextualized","scope":"language","statement":"A concept like status or iteration can be a generic class, with the particular algorithm it belongs to known from restricted."},{"id":"L-abstract-algebra","scope":"other","statement":"Luthier has to do with abstract algebra."},{"id":"L-sharing-platform","scope":"other","statement":"Luthier is a platform where code."},{"id":"L-definition-is-its-test","scope":"language","statement":"Defining a function defines its test (its inverse, its simulation), so running the code runs the test."},{"id":"L-levels-of-verification","scope":"language","statement":"A value can be untested or tested, with different levels of verification."},{"id":"L-luthierize-foreign-code","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier annotates and 'luthierizes' foreign code, verifying it against the definition of what it should do within some {"new_lineages":[{"id":"L-compiling-detects-errors","scope":"language","statement":"Compiling is checking whether the code holds incompatible things; unlike algebraic calculation, many programs should not compile, because that is how errors are caught."},{"id":"L-library-adapter","scope":"language","statement":"A library is used by requiring it follow patterns and satisfy propositions defined from Luthier, with an adapter fitting it to each use, so Luthier acts as a universal adapter between libraries."},{"id":"L-apply-luthier-to-[private word]","scope":"method","statement":"Luthier's concepts (function plus version, a table of functions) are carried into the design of the analysis/derivation store."},{"id":"L-result-type-closed","scope":"language","statement":"Each function declares a result type with fixed fields; the set of result types is open but every individual type is closed, a sum of types, not a JSON blob."},{"id":"L-schema-from-type","scope":"language","statement":"The storage schema is generated from the function's declared type rather than written by hand, and migration is derived."},{"id":"L-derived-is-proof-term","scope":"language","statement":"A derived object, the tuple of inputs, function, parameters and result, is a proof term whose type is the proposition that the result was obtained that way, making the base a store of proofs."},{"id":"L-verify-by-sampling","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier verifies postconditions by sampling possible inputs, and postcondition verification and coverage calibration are the same computation."},{"id":"L-precondition-is-type","scope":"language","statement":"A precondition is guaranteed by the argument's type, checked when the reference is formed; preconditions that are predicates over values require refined types."},{"id":"L-original-vs-derivative-types","scope":"method","statement":"Some types are original (made from audios and questionnaires) and all the rest are derivative, results of functions, so they necessarily have structure."},{"id":"L-function-deterministic","scope":"method","statement":"If the identity of a derived object is its inputs, function, version and parameters, the function must be deterministic: seed and environment enter as explicit arguments, or the certificate lies."},{"id":"L-derived-never-edited","scope":"method","statement":"A derived object is never edited; dato, subtipo, aplicar, reducir."},{"id":"L-two-luthier-own","scope":"language","statement":"Of the core elements eight are standard type theory and two are Luthier's own: the hole as a first-class packaging."},{"id":"L-base-predicate-design-decision","scope":"language","statement":"Where the base type ends and predicates begin is a design decision that fixes what is computation and what is data."},{"id":"L-cross-representation-is-function","scope":"language","statement":"When two types have different representations their relation is always a certified function with laws, never a subtype and never an implicit coercion; injecting the integers into the reals does not make them reals."},{"id":"L-natural-vs-predicative-detail","scope":"language","statement":"Semantically the difference between a natural type and a predicative (subtype) type looks like an implementation detail."},{"id":"L-data-or-subtype-rule","scope":"language","statement":"Use data when the thing has its own form and operations, a subtype when it restricts something that already has operations; both are types of equal status, one carrying a certificate and the other not."},{"id":"L-subtype-name-is-interface","scope":"language","statement":"A named subtype and its long set-builder form are the same by definition; the name is the interface and nobody writes the long form."},{"id":"L-extern-is-labeled-hole","scope":"language","statement":"extern is a hole with a label saying who fills it, the border between what runs by hand and what does not, and could be an ordinary library function rather than a keyword."},{"id":"L-explicit-errors","scope":"language","statement":"Maybe_error<T> was useful but errors should be made more explicit, with the worry that this breeds complex dynamic types."},{"id":"L-error-type-computed-by-verifier","scope":"language","statement":"The error sum of composed functions is an ordinary type the verifier computes from their types, not dynamic nor dependent, with error growth managed by exact sum inside and forgetting at borders."},{"id":"L-possible-vs-occurred-error","scope":"language","statement":"The type of possible error (computed before running, small and linear) is distinct from the error that occurred (computed at run time, a datum of variable structure)."},{"id":"L-error-as-failure-tree","scope":"language","statement":"Error is a single recursive Failure type, a tree of label, argument and sub-failures whose labels are quotes of program mechanical."},{"id":"L-iteration-propagation","scope":"language","statement":"Iteration whose length comes from a datum is the common case (MCMC), and what to design are three forms of propagation, eval."},{"id":"L-define-and-test-structure","scope":"language","statement":"The two things wanted of an algebraic structure are to define what it is and to test whether a particular implementation {"new_lineages":[{"id":"L-module-is-record","scope":"language","statement":"A module is a record whose components are its definitions, so qualifying with the dot is the same as projecting."},{"id":"L-design-approval-before-code","scope":"method","statement":"Before implementing anything the model describes the design and waits for approval before writing tests."},{"id":"L-sampler-likelihood-kernel","scope":"language","statement":"Sampler and likelihood are two readings of one Markov kernel, related as adjoint operators rather than adjoint functors."},{"id":"L-mutual-test-chain","scope":"language","statement":"The MAP is tested with the likelihood as the likelihood is tested with the sampler, a closed chain where the algorithm produces argument."},{"id":"L-native-extern-agree","scope":"language","statement":"Each concept is written twice, native in Luthier as the slow conceptual reference and extern in Python as the fast version, parts."},{"id":"L-array-primitive","scope":"language","statement":"Arrays (Vec, Mat) enter as a primitive certified by algebraic laws with generators, with accessors and tabulate so Python traverses while Luthier still sees values, the conceptual endpoint being a dimension-indexed Vec : Nat -> U."},{"id":"L-no-exact-equality-floats","scope":"language","statement":"== does not decide over floats or arrays; comparison is an approximate relation with a tolerance (tolOf n = 8 n eps, the slack declared once)."},{"id":"L-environment-evaluator","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier's evaluator of L squared restricted to the tangent space and the gaussian model a map between inner-product spaces."},{"id":"L-shift-retraction","scope":"language","statement":"shift moves a parameter in a {"new_lineages":[
{"id":"L-code-over-declared-generic","scope":"language","statement":"Native code over a merely-declared type is no longer legal and must become generic (the ML functor), and cycle detection forces reading the whole file before typing."},
{"id":"L-labels-are-binders","scope":"language","statement":"Record labels are binding names like parameter names, so a labelled record is the Sigma chain with named binders and labels do not enter the type's identity."},
{"id":"L-shape-before-laws","scope":"language","statement":"A type's shape must be fixed in its declaration before its laws, since the laws are written over its components and must be typed before the type closes."},
{"id":"L-type-vs-value-mark","scope":"language","statement":"Whether a definition declares a value (an inhabitant) or a subtype is resolved by the body's type, not by a distinct symbol."},
{"id":"L-value-is-type-single-inhabitant","scope":"language","statement":"Eliminate the type/value distinction: everything is a type and a value is a type with a single inhabitant, with x : T meaning x refines T."},
{"id":"L-eval-determination-run-test","scope":"language","statement":"Evaluating a predicate on determined names is running and on non-determined names is testing: the same evaluator under a different determination."},
{"id":"L-determined-is-reducing-body","scope":"language","statement":"A body computes while a law only verifies, so \"determined\" in practice means having a body or extern that reduces."},
{"id":"L-extern-provisional","scope":"language","statement":"An extern over a not-yet-defined type is marked provisional so the debt stays visible, recorded in the certificate rather than treated as a verdict."},
{"id":"L-opaque-body-is-laws","scope":"language","statement":"An opaque type's body is the conjunction of the laws over it and its operations, so every object has a head (a type whose body names the laws) and there are no free-standing laws that define."},
{"id":"L-object-is-theory-presentation","scope":"language","statement":"A mathematical object is a theory never written; what one writes are presentations (cycles with laws, by observers, constructors, or both) and certified translations between them are the evidence that two presentations are the same object."},
{"id":"L-constructors-are-generator","scope":"language","statement":"When a type is presented by constructors tied to observers by laws, the constructors are its generator, which comes for free by composing them."},
{"id":"L-translation-second-order","scope":"language","statement":"A translation between two presentations of a structure is a second-order Luthier concept, quantifying over presentations (type operators U -> U), expressible and checkable in Luthier itself."},
{"id":"L-luthier-self-presentations","scope":"language","statement":"Luthier itself admits several equivalent primitive presentations (it already has three), one chosen as canonical by whether 04's static semantics can be stated directly on it rather than by minimality, while the checker may keep a richer one for speed."},
{"id":"L-translation-certified-per-model","scope":"language","statement":"A translation quantified over all carriers and models cannot be tested without a model generator, so it is certified per concrete model, not in general."},
{"id":"L-translation-inherits-laws","scope":"language","statement":"When a translation returns a value in the target presentation, the target's laws become an obligation that the translated model inherits and discharges."},
{"id":"L-equality-as-component","scope":"language","statement":"Each presentation must supply its own observational equality as a component, parametrized and eventually probabilistic, returning a verdict with its level rather than a fixed Bool."},
{"id":"L-object-as-record-type","scope":"language","statement":"An object is always a record type defined by its laws that includes its carrier, so the cycle always exists, implementations are its values, and giving a name both a law-body and an extern-body is two bodies forbidden by one := per name."},
{"id":"L-vec-not-primitive","scope":"language","statement":"Vec is not a semantic primitive but a function from a finite index to R written with Pi and subtype, with tabulate as constructor and at as observer; it only seems primitive for performance, separating semantic primitives (the kernel) from performance primitives (externs)."},
{"id":"L-real-vs-theoretical-objects","scope":"language","statement":"There are real objects with constructors (native types) and theoretical ones without (parametrized record types whose constructors are their models); both should exist and which is meant must be explicit."},
{"id":"L-sufficient-completeness","scope":"language","statement":"Laws never determine a unique implementation and need not; aim at sufficient completeness (one law per observer-constructor cell plus extensionality), checkable mechanically, so the object is determined up to isomorphism."},
{"id":"L-law-independence-witnessed","scope":"language","statement":"A law is independent if a model exists satisfying all the others and violating it, an existential tested by a negative control, the witnessed verdict left open in 04."},
{"id":"L-table-dependent-function","scope":"language","statement":"A Table is a dependent function from column and row to cell whose cell type depends on the column, with fromColumns as constructor and application as observer."},
{"id":"L-firm-bases-first","scope":"method","statement":"First make Luthier's bases firm and complete in the sense discussed, and only once that is decided revise everything so those bases hold."},
{"id":"L-spec-by-executing","scope":"method","statement":"Pure waterfall is wrong, since the rules changed repeatedly and inconsistencies surfaced only from writing concrete examples; each decision is written as accept/reject pairs in an executable spec suite and the interpreter changed until it passes, the law holding only when a concrete case tests it."},

{"new_lineages":[{"id":"L-constructors-freely-generated","scope":"language","statement":"Constructors of an inductive type are freely generated with no equations, so the Peano disequalities (disjoint, succ injective, succ n distinct from n) are free theorems that survive without definition."},{"id":"L-recursor-in-core","scope":"language","statement":"Whether the recursor is a core primitive: keep when a model is given."},{"id":"L-structural-types-primitive","scope":"language","statement":"Product, sum and exponential of types are made language primitives with their named record {..} and freedom) or laws (refinement) generate a new named type; a product or sum without laws deserves no new name."},{"id":"L-rules-as-errors-no-migration","scope":"method","statement":"Rather than migrate old code behind a --strict flag, do not migrate it so the rules apply as errors from day one and each rewritten library is a pilot of the spec."},{"id":"L-rewrite-useful-new-syntax","scope":"method","statement":"Take what is useful or theoretically elegant from the existing .lut and rewrite it under the new syntax."},{"id":"L-rewrite-regression-numbers","scope":"method","statement":"The rewritten experiment_zero must reproduce the same numbers on session A (σ 25.6 cm with everything, 4.9 cm without parlante_A2) as a concrete regression."},{"id":"L-generic-vs-project-location","scope":"method","statement":"Generic libraries live in luthier/lib and project-specific files in sonolocalización, ending the duplicated copies that caused confusion."},{"id":"L-table-accessor-partial","scope":"language","statement":"A table accessor returning a default (0, 0.0, \"\") where a column is missing is a partial function in disguise, guarded by the schema invariants rather than the type."},{"id":"L-certify-reloads-per-name","scope":"method","statement":"Certification is slow because the script reloads and rechecks everything once per name; running all obligations of a file in one invocation would fix it."},{"id":"L-pattern-bound-not-quantified","scope":"language","statement":"Obligations under a tuple pattern of any length are not quantified over the named components, but obligations under a constructor pattern still quantify over all of its argument."},{"id":"L-right-association-bit-equality","scope":"language","statement":"Summation and the product of types associate to the right, like the tuple, which is what enabled bit-for-bit {"new_lineages":[{"id":"L-real-realized-by-float64","scope":"language","statement":"Real is not implemented but delegated to Float64, which realizes it at runtime as an interpreter choice recorded in the certificate."},{"id":"L-nan-inf-not-reals","scope":"language","statement":"Since Float64 is a Real, NaN and overflow to infinity are always errors, and a meaningful infinity is requested in the type via ExtendedReal."},{"id":"L-discrete-output-distribution","scope":"language","statement":"When a probabilistic path makes the output discrete (a rank, stop reason, count), the result type must be able to say it is a distribution over outcomes."},{"id":"L-array-generic-element-type","scope":"language","statement":"Array is generic in the element type with numeric operations over Real (Vec = Array Real), so index arrays become Array Int and writing it over Float64 would reglue definition to realization."},{"id":"L-leaf-declared-over-float64","scope":"language","statement":"An extern leaf is declared over what it really receives and returns (Vec Float64, not Real), since the type cannot affirm what the implementation does not deliver, forcing libraries generic in the number type."},{"id":"L-function-subtyping-float64","scope":"language","statement":"The function subtyping rule (domain contravariant, codomain covariant) accepts the argument and promotes the Float64 a leaf returns to Real, with an explicit toFloat64 where a Real must be rounded."},{"id":"L-real-carrier-plus-axiom","scope":"language","statement":"Real is written as carrier plus structure, Real := primitive and realField : CompleteOrderedField Real := axiom, where axiom is a value whose laws are assumed."},{"id":"L-law-in-hole-declaration","scope":"language","statement":"The law belongs in the hole's declaration so filling it with the extern inherits the obligation and every use of the name is a certified value, removing the duplicated certified copies."},{"id":"L-leaf-not-certified-via-another-leaf","scope":"language","statement":"A leaf's certification tolerance should use the native definition, not another leaf, so no leaf certifies itself by leaning on another."},{"id":"L-ad-hoc-laws-reproduce-implementation","scope":"language","statement":"The objects-as-types-with-laws theory is not used in the key cases (Vec, Table, Mat, Objective); ad hoc laws reproduce the function's implementation instead of stating the mathematical invariants that characterize it."},{"id":"L-law-characterizes-not-reimplements","scope":"language","statement":"A law states the mathematical property that determines an operation up to the presentation's equality; a second implementation is consistency not characterization, and the native definition is one more model certified against it."},{"id":"L-one-name-per-thing","scope":"language","statement":"Do not declare the same thing under two distinct names."},{"id":"L-algebra-always-imported","scope":"language","statement":"The algebra library must always be imported because it is the base of all the properties."},{"id":"L-best-math-object-as-invariant","scope":"language","statement":"For every concept, find the mathematical object that best represents it and put it as the type's invariant rather than merely stating it."},{"id":"L-symmetric-matrix-vs-operation","scope":"language","statement":"A symmetric matrix and a symmetric operation are distinct things, though a symmetric matrix obeys symmetric laws."},{"id":"L-symmetric-matrix-type","scope":"language","statement":"Spectral operations must take a Symmetric type (with a tolerance, since numpy's inverses are not exactly symmetric), putting the mathematical precondition in the type that the code was lying about."},{"id":"L-folds-are-monoid-fold","scope":"language","statement":"The folds over Fin n (sumTo, totalDef, maxOver, forallBelow, listLength) are all the same monoid fold and should be one right-associated fold."},{"id":"L-shift-is-action","scope":"language","statement":"shift is an action of the tangent space on Theta (an affine space), with ShiftByZero as its left identity and ShiftComposes its associativity, carried as invariant by MeanModel/Likelihood."},{"id":"L-position-encodings-iso","scope":"language","statement":"The three encodings of the positions are tied by no law though flatten is an Iso, and the gauge should be one injection with the rest derived."},{"id":"L-shapes-preconditions-in-types","scope":"language","statement":"The leaves do not carry their shape or range preconditions in their types (matVec accepts any shape, missing range checks), which should become dependent invariants."},{"id":"L-equalities-should-be-setoid","scope":"language","statement":"Loose equalities like BeliefFamily.same and Codec.eq should be Setoid instances."},{"id":"L-table-by-schema-laws","scope":"language","statement":"Table becomes a type defined by the laws of its schema, with accessors carrying the column as a precondition, though the schema laws are not verified over the tables Python returns."},{"id":"L-abs-returns-nonnegative","scope":"language","statement":"abs returns a NonNegative, backed by its law."},{"id":"L-normalvec-uniform-law","scope":"language","statement":"normalVec gets a law for the first time: its integral transform is uniform."},{"id":"L-objective-laws","scope":"language","statement":"Objective carries its laws: the gradient is that of its value and the step matrix is positive semidefinite, plus the laws of any maximizer."},{"id":"L-bool-read-by-position","scope":"language","statement":"Bool is read by position, so any sum of two Units counts as Bool with the first alternative true, and a predicate that always returns the wrong label passes."},{"id":"L-stale-certificates-not-pruned","scope":"language","statement":"Certificate entries only accumulate and old ones are never pruned, so reading the file one cannot tell current from obsolete without recomputing the hashes."},{"id":"L-acoustic-stage-drives-next","scope":"method","statement":"The next Luthier work should be pushed by the acoustic stage and the GCC likelihood, not the cleanup of the algebra."},{"id":"L-exhaustive-int-is-small-range","scope":"language","statement":"\"Exhaustive\" over Int means only the range -16 to 16, so a law is certified exhaustive on 33 cases that are not exhaustive."},{"id":"L-field-laws-pass-by-tuned-magnitude","scope":"language","statement":"The field laws of float64Field pass only because lawMagnitude is tuned to the generator range; associativity fails at (1e8, -1e8, 3e-9) and the type does not state the box."},{"id":"L-hardcode-twice-across-bridge","scope":"language","statement":"Fixed facts like the gauge nodes are written twice across the Python/Luthier bridge, breaking one-name-per-thing and the no-hardcoding rule."},{"id":"L-generator-ignores-refinement","scope":"language","statement":"The generator does not respect dependent refinements, producing false failures because the obligation was quantified over the base type, not the refined one."},{"id":"L-cert-hash-misses-python","scope":"language","statement":"The certificate hash covers only the extern's text, not the Python source, generator, case count or interpreter version, so editing lm.py leaves the certificate current."},{"id":"L-pending-recorded-as-fail","scope":"language","statement":"A law that cannot be run (no generator, out of fuel, pending over a theory) is recorded as FAIL, mixed with real counterexamples."},{"id":"L-provisional-externs-certified","scope":"language","statement":"Provisional externs are certified although R5 forbids it, and the certificate carries no provisional field."},{"id":"L-bridge-ignores-declared-type","scope":"language","statement":"The Python bridge turns any int, float or str into a literal regardless of the declared type, and division follows the Python type, so an Int disguised as Float64 gives integer division."},{"id":"L-real-only-a-label","scope":"language","statement":"Real exists only at type-checking with no representation or generator and arithmetic over it rejected; the libraries are Float64 end to end, so the distinction yields nothing today."},{"id":"L-run-record-omits-uncertified-cone","scope":"language","statement":"Spec 05 asks the run record to note the uncertified names of the cone, but the CLI saves only entry, hash, when, parameters and result."},{"id":"L-setoid-caught-real-bug","scope":"method","statement":"Typing same as a Setoid caught a real bug (the gaussian belief was not symmetric), the best evidence that the method catches errors."},{"id":"L-certs-on-holes-never-match","scope":"language","statement":"Certificates depending on holes never match because the hash is compared at import before the parent fills the holes but was computed after."},{"id":"L-runs-not-what-certified","scope":"language","statement":"What runs (10 nodes, full vector) is not what was certified (7 nodes, gauge); the transfer rests on an informal argument no law states and the checker ignores."},{"id":"L-dome-gcc-externs","scope":"language","statement":"The dome and GCC-PHAT with thousands of samples cannot be native given the speed and will be externs end to end."},{"id":"L-certification-impl-broken","scope":"method","statement":"The certification machinery does not do what spec 05 promises (failing certs, stale ones, generators ignoring refinements, what runs not what was certified) and should be fixed before the next library rewrite."},{"id":"L-slow-nested-op-inference","scope":"language","statement":"Loading anything importing array.lut takes ~17-19s because each nested + or * re-infers the left operand's type."},{"id":"L-certs-internal-not-empirical","scope":"method","statement":"Nothing is applied to the real data; the certificates speak of internal coherence, not of whether the model describes the measurements."},{"id":"L-refined-codomain-no-obligation","scope":"language","statement":"A refined codomain on an extern's type produces no obligation; neg : Float64 -> NonNeg can return -2.0 unchecked."},{"id":"L-project-constants-leak","scope":"language","statement":"Project-specific constants calibrated to the tape (pitTol, ensembleSize, zMax, fdStep) leak into the generic library instead of being parameters."},{"id":"L-interpreted-likelihood-slow","scope":"language","statement":"A 30-parameter fit takes 3 minutes because the cost is the interpreted likelihood."},{"id":"L-two-evaluators-diverge","scope":"language","statement":"There are two evaluators that differ in edge cases, and the machine silently falls back to the substitution one."},{"id":"L-ergonomics-let-unary-minus","scope":"language","statement":"Writing costs for lack of let, implicit arguments and unary minus (functions end in ten closing braces), which should come before any kernel refinement."},{"id":"L-guarantees-in-comments","scope":"language","statement":"Guarantees live in comments instead of in types (meanModel says its inputs are nodes but MapInput carries Vec Int unrelated to Node)."},{"id":"L-cert-grades-not-implemented","scope":"language","statement":"The certificate grades spec 05 promises (point, witnessed, assumed, weakest link of a chain) are not implemented."},{"id":"L-statistical-tests-low-power","scope":"method","statement":"The statistical tests have low power: few cases and controls that break the model at double sigma, the easiest case to detect, so a 10-20% error in sigma may go undetected."},{"id":"L-equality-check-holes","scope":"language","statement":"R8 has holes: == is accepted over data containing functions, over Real as float equality, and not checked past depth 20."},{"id":"L-fix-certification-as-gate","scope":"method","statement":"Freeze v0 and commit, then fix certification as a gate (generators respecting refinements, pending distinct from failure, delete entries without a current name, record the uncertified cone)."},{"id":"L-int-tables-as-float","scope":"language","statement":"Fin n -> Int tables are generated as float64 against spec 06, so integer laws over indices run with floating-point {"id":"L-dimension-in-types","scope":"language","statement":"The model's dimension must enter the types of probability, belief and optimization (Theta is VecOf n throughout), since with an unconstrained Vec Float64 the model's obligations were false."},
{"id":"L-exception-skips-obligation","scope":"language","statement":"A type obligation speaks of the values a computation produces, so an exception yields no value and that case is skipped, whereas a law stated in a definition's type keeps failing on an exception."},
{"id":"L-constants-must-be-parameters","scope":"language","statement":"A criterion hardcoded as a constant in the code (lmMaxIter, the rejection-sampler's try budget) must be a parameter, by the rule that every criterion is a parameter."},
{"id":"L-generic-laws-dont-run","scope":"language","statement":"Laws generic in a type parameter (Theta : U) never run because there is no generator of U, so they are certified only when a program fills the hole with a concrete type that has a generator, or by a well-chosen instance, and asking for a generator of U is a static error."},
{"id":"L-hole-no-default","scope":"language","statement":"In Luthier a hole has no default, so each run must supply every parameter by --set; a parameter with a default value that --set replaces and the run records would be a new language feature."},
{"id":"L-statistical-law-level-retry","scope":"language","statement":"A statistical law declares its level (the probability of failing on a correct model), is retried with an independent seed before a failure counts as a counterexample (level alpha squared), and reports a verdict with that level rather than a bare pass/fail."},
{"id":"L-checker-loses-laws-in-branches","scope":"language","statement":"When the expected type has laws the checker does not inspect each branch of an if or match; it infers the type of the whole, loses the laws and raises one obligation over the whole expression."},
{"id":"L-problem-vs-objective","scope":"language","statement":"negate falsely promises an Objective with laws from arbitrary functions, so a lawless Problem (what the algorithm runs) is split from an Objective (a Problem with laws) and negate returns a Problem, making the obligation disappear."},
{"id":"L-square-no-generator","scope":"language","statement":"Square has no registered generator, so a square matrix is drawn by rejection (one in seventeen), a cost paid per case by every law with a Square parameter; it needs a real gen Square."},
{"id":"L-generation-part-of-certificate","scope":"language","statement":"Unless a gen is declared the tester builds values from the type's structure, and that construction is part of what each certificate means and silently decides what a law actually tests; generators are checked for being in the type, never for covering it."},
{"id":"L-generator-explicit-per-type","scope":"language","statement":"There is no single generator per type, so a test must name the explicit generator it bound to each type and the certificate records it (gen T := disappears); functions are generated by a census over registered values."},
{"id":"L-interval-arithmetic-bounded-real","scope":"language","statement":"Interval arithmetic fits Luthier because its correctness is a single inclusion law Luthier can already certify: a bounded Real is a certificate carried across a computation that yields a bound for a function's values."},
{"id":"L-check-refines-value-type","scope":"language","statement":"A check done on a value refines its type (inside if p x, x has the refined type) so nobody checks it again, with the result's granularity chosen by the cost of redoing it; this applies to run results, which are checked once into the run record."},
{"id":"L-check-bool-primary-derived","scope":"language","statement":"A check is written once as a Bool (the law, composing by and/or/not) with refinement by branch as the rule, and the refined type and other presentations are derived."},
{"id":"L-certifying-algorithm-witness","scope":"language","statement":"A certifying algorithm returns its result plus a witness a simple checker verifies, the refined value being the special case where the witness is the value itself, giving in general a dependent pair with a law."},
{"id":"L-refine-reading-not-path","scope":"language","statement":"When the checked fact is external, refining the value gives a guarantee that can expire, so the principle refines what was read, not the reference, and check and use must be the same operation."},
{"id":"L-tolerance-checks-dont-compose","scope":"language","statement":"Checks with a tolerance do not compose, since a near b and b near c do not give a near c at the same tolerance, so if used to refine, the tolerance must go in the type."},
{"id":"L-monad-vs-applicative-validation","scope":"language","statement":"A monad stops at the first failure (fit for a pipeline) while validating by hand wants the full list of violations (an applicative that accumulates errors), and the context decides between the two."},
{"id":"L-pi-stays-with-luciano","scope":"method","statement":"The principal-investigator role in Luthier stays with Luciano because the design decisions are his, and an agent runs only subproblems with a mechanical acceptance criterion, since Luthier's mechanical verifier is stronger than a code-reading agent."},
{"id":"L-certificates-enable-autonomy","scope":"method","statement":"Luthier's mechanical certificates and file-held state let the AI work sustainedly through the night and across context compaction, since a pass/fail certificate makes it prudent to run the check and continue."},
{"id":"L-phase-states-closing-check","scope":"method","statement":"Each phase of a plan should state what check closes it, and a phase with no mechanical check belongs to Luciano and not to the autonomous run."},
{"id":"L-mechanize-rules-lint-hook","scope":"method","statement":"The instructions living in memory are moved to mechanical checks in three layers (what Luthier can reject, what a repo lint catches, what stays judgment with a mechanical reminder), which requires relaxing the rule that only Luciano runs the scripts for lints and certification."},
{"id":"L-concurrent-session-commit","scope":"method","statement":"With another session committing in the same repo, the model leaves its changes uncommitted and first looks at what the other session touched so its work is not swept into a commit with a different message."},
{"id":"L-certify-full-design-fisher","scope":"language","statement":"The density-pair laws are certified over the full design (all pairs of the seven nodes) rather than over sampled graphs, because they need a non-singular Fisher information that the session-A graph does not provide."},
{"id":"L-cert-guarantees-via-typed-externs","scope":"language","statement":"A certificate now guarantees something because every value returned from Python is read by its declared type, and the certificate hash covers the Luthier code, the Python behind each extern and the interpreter."},
{"id":"L-objective-from-list","scope":"language","statement":"An Objective should not be drawn by rejection (random functions almost never match their declared gradient) but taken from an explicit list of registered values, such as the project's own objective and a quadratic."},
{"id":"L-reuse-not-run-law-result","scope":"language","statement":"Re-running a not-run law is wasted work when code, generators and seed are the same, since the result is deterministic, so the tester could reuse that result as it reuses a certificate."},
{"id":"L-number-generator-limits-scale","scope":"language","statement":"A number generator needs explicit limit values and a linear or logarithmic scale (with special values and their weight), the limits carried in the type, so a Float64 without limits in its type is a static error if the binding does not supply them."},
{"id":"L-binding-by-parameter","scope":"language","statement":"Each quantified variable is paired with its generator by parameter, the only thing that distinguishes tol from an input of the mean, with profiles serving as abbreviation."},
{"id":"L-generator-is-luthier-value","scope":"language","statement":"A generator is a Luthier value with its own type and laws, certifiable like any other, and the random number generator is an extern with its stochasticity laws declared in Luthier."},
{"id":"L-polymorphic-one-instance","scope":"language","statement":"For a broad class of polymorphic properties it suffices to test one well-chosen instance (Bernardy, Jansson and Claessen 2010)."},
{"id":"L-inverse-cdf-sampling","scope":"language","statement":"Sampling by the cumulative sum of costs is inverse-CDF sampling, one primitive for the continuous case (linear or log) and the finite census, with exhaustive over an infinite type a static error."},
{"id":"L-run-inputs-vs-cert-reach","scope":"language","statement":"A run's inputs are compared against the reach of the certificates: what arrives via --set at startup, and what is computed during the run only under --checked."}

L-abs-returns-nonnegative.statement: abs returns a NonNegative, backed by its law.

L-absolute-vs-local-coords.statement: A situated object carries two coordinate systems with distinct roles, absolute (GPS/datetime) fixing identity and hash since two objects cannot share a place and time, and local for inference, joined by a Frame with a consistency law; both kinds of type are needed.

L-abstract-algebra.statement: Luthier has to do with abstract algebra.

L-abstract-machine-certify.statement: An abstract machine is an interpreter whose state is a datum, the most convenient way to certify one interpreter against another by comparing states step by step rather than only results.

L-abstraction-mechanism.statement: Luthier is an abstraction mechanism, a relator, for expressing ideas clearly (probability, sample, matrix, units, experiment).

L-academic-language-excludes.statement: Academic language communicates easily among academics but blocks outsiders, a jargon of exclusivity, academics being a parasite society feeds that returns an internal skeleton.

L-accumulates-without-advancing.statement: Luthier keeps accumulating ideas without starting to advance, tending to grow to encompass the universe, attractive but like a bag of gas.

L-acoustic-stage-drives-next.statement: The next Luthier work should be pushed by the acoustic stage and the GCC likelihood, not the cleanup of the algebra.

L-acritical-amplifier.statement: The Luthier AI acted as an acritical amplifier, celebrating every idea without flagging contradictions or the state of the art.

L-ad-hoc-laws-reproduce-implementation.statement: The objects-as-types-with-laws theory is not used in the key cases (Vec, Table, Mat, Objective); ad hoc laws reproduce the function's implementation instead of stating the mathematical invariants that characterize it.

L-adjoint-forward-diagnostic.statement: Each forward operation (simulate, infer) is paired by adjunction with a diagnostic approximation (recover, summarize).

L-against-pure-waterfall.statement: Pure waterfall fails: the rule changed three times and the two-bodies inconsistency surfaced only from writing a concrete example; specs written without executing err where no one imagined.

L-agnostic-program-universe-state.statement: The language should not distinguish types that speak of the program's internal state from those that speak of the universe's state; the program should be agnostic.

L-ai-output-exceeds-processing.statement: The AI generates information faster than he can process it, flooding and clogging him, so forms of synthesis are needed.

L-ai-to-condense-dispersion.statement: Use the AI to help synthesize and condense his own dispersion, consolidating a mass of ideas into polished ones by a protocol.

L-algebra-always-imported.statement: The algebra library must always be imported because it is the base of all the properties.

L-algebra-chooses-number-object.statement: Rather than rewrite floating-point arithmetic, use algebra to choose the mathematical object that best represents the reals.

L-algebraic-and-semantic.statement: Luthier should have a very algebraic way of writing itself that can express almost anything like a universal Turing machine, yet where each element is semantically defined and understandable by humans.

L-alias-equals-not-coloneq.statement: Naming a product (AB = A*B) is an abbreviation expanded before verification with no states; naming it with := is rejected, with = it is an alias.

L-alias-invariant-in-generator.statement: An apparent alias like Perturbed hides its real invariant in the generator rather than the type; the new rules expose it.

L-almacen-is-constructor-function.statement: A structure like Almacen is a function that takes the raw operations and returns the verified versions, so the only way to obtain one is to pass the check.

L-analysis-only-at-moments.statement: The whole verification apparatus is expensive parafernalia layered on top, so one must be able to say it runs only at some moments, not always.

L-apply-luthier-to-[private word].statement: Luthier's concepts (function plus version, a table of functions) are carried into the design of the analysis/derivation store.

L-approxring-eps.statement: Floats are not a ring but satisfy the laws of a distinct subtype with a tolerance parameter eps in the type, and the exact ring is that subtype at eps=0 rather than an independent definition.

L-arena-or-lambda-calculus.statement: Luthier can grow as a universal arena or, more simply, as a down-to-earth lambda calculus.

L-argument-domains.statement: A Domain is defined for each function argument so sets of arguments can be sampled from it.

L-array-generic-element-type.statement: Array is generic in the element type with numeric operations over Real (Vec = Array Real), so index arrays become Array Int and writing it over Float64 would reglue definition to realization.

L-array-laws-missing.statement: array.lut uses the opaque Vec/at/tabulate pattern but the laws defining Vec are written nowhere, so numpy fills holes untied by any law, which R3 would reject.

L-array-primitive.statement: Arrays (Vec, Mat) enter as a primitive certified by algebraic laws with generators, with accessors and tabulate so Python traverses while Luthier still sees values, the conceptual endpoint being a dimension-indexed Vec : Nat -> U.

L-ascii-canonical.statement: The canonical form of the language is ASCII; an editor may display -> as an arrow or * as a cross, but what is run by hand and grepped is the ASCII.

L-atomic-laws.statement: Compound laws like Identity and Distributive are split into left and right atomic laws so each can fail separately, with the structure's components a product the predicate runs over.

L-backward-forward-evaluation.statement: Two ways of working, backward (lazy, starting from what is asked) and forward (compute everything, markovian with no past), each with its role.

L-base-vs-predicate-line.statement: The distinction between a base type and a predicate is structural, but where the base ends and predicates begin is a design decision that decides what is computation and what is data.

L-based-on-hott.statement: Build Luthier to map strictly onto homotopy type theory, with very few types following its small set of well-defined rules.

L-bases-firm-first.statement: First make Luthier's bases firm and complete, and only once decided revise everything so those bases hold, a waterfall approach.

L-bayesian-complexity-estimate.statement: The a priori complexity of implementations is estimated by a Bayesian strategy: give chances to different algorithms, measure their actual times, and estimate from accumulated experience.

L-bayesian-mapping.statement: Scientific knowledge production is mapped into explicit Bayesian structures (introduction to prior, methods to likelihood, results to observations, discussion to posterior) to make reasoning auditable and probabilistic.

L-bayesian-verification-regime.statement: Verification is read as a Bayesian observer updating what it knows by what it observes, with proof, exhaustive and assumed at the logical limit of probabilities 0 and 1 and sampling where the rest enters.

L-belief-prior-posterior.statement: Prior and posterior are one state of knowledge about theta (a Belief with a cursor over the data) updated by one operation; the gaussian belief in information form closes under the Laplace update so the MAP is how that update is implemented, and null-eigenvalue precision is an improper belief for rigid directions.

L-best-math-object-as-invariant.statement: For every concept, find the mathematical object that best represents it and put it as the type's invariant rather than merely stating it.

L-binding-by-parameter.statement: Each quantified variable is paired with its generator by parameter, the only thing that distinguishes tol from an input of the mean, with profiles serving as abbreviation.

L-block-is-program.statement: Braces delimit a block that can hold local definitions; a block is a Program with one definition marked as output, giving local definitions without new primitives.

L-body-type-resolves-ambiguity.statement: Whether a definition gives a value or a subtype is resolved by the body's type (T vs T->Bool), not by a symbol.

L-bool-read-by-position.statement: Bool is read by position, so any sum of two Units counts as Bool with the first alternative true, and a predicate that always returns the wrong label passes.

L-bootstrap-pact.statement: The only thing outside Luthier is a bootstrap that accepts a Program value, parses it and runs eval; once eval written in Luthier runs on itself the bootstrapper can be discarded, which is the concrete self-extensibility.

L-bridge-ignores-declared-type.statement: The Python bridge turns any int, float or str into a literal regardless of the declared type, and division follows the Python type, so an Int disguised as Float64 gives integer division.

L-bridge-language.statement: Luthier should be minimal, essentially a bridge language connecting other languages.

L-brokentext-needs-grammar.statement: Giving BrokenText an honest predicate requires the format's grammar written in Luthier, which today only the Python parser has.

L-build-before-it-falls.statement: Luthier must be built now, before access to highly qualified AI guidance becomes restricted.

L-butler-orchestrator.statement: Luthier is a higher-order language, a butler that orchestrates other languages, runs programs, compares their outputs, and chooses where to run each computation.

L-candidate-named-not-forall.statement: The candidate value is named and the laws applied to it explicitly, but it has the material's type (naming it by the subtype is circular) and needs no forall; the sample size is certificate data, not part of the type.

L-cartesian-closed.statement: Product, sum and exponential of types are missing to make Luthier a cartesian closed category.

L-category-style-basics.statement: The basic elements are defined in category-theory style, functors from arrows, out of a few basal elements.

L-cert-grades-not-implemented.statement: The certificate grades spec 05 promises (point, witnessed, assumed, weakest link of a chain) are not implemented.

L-cert-guarantees-via-typed-externs.statement: A certificate now guarantees something because every value returned from Python is read by its declared type, and the certificate hash covers the Luthier code, the Python behind each extern and the interpreter.

L-cert-hash-misses-python.statement: The certificate hash covers only the extern's text, not the Python source, generator, case count or interpreter version, so editing lm.py leaves the certificate current.

L-certificate-clause-with-hypotheses.statement: A certificate is a clause with hypotheses (H1 and ... and Hn imply L), and a program's certificate is the closure of those clauses, which gives composition its exact meaning.

L-certificate-first-class.statement: The certificate is a first-class value carrying its level of guarantee, composable and forgettable, accumulating by composition across values, functions and programs, with runs persisted as data.

L-certificate-is-only-a-record.statement: The certificate neither enables nor blocks anything, it is only a record, so the word certificate is excessive.

L-certificate-reproducible.statement: A certificate that does not record the seed, generation parameters and domain of each variable is not reproducible, so one seed per run is chosen and stored, each definition's derived from it, and --seed repeats the whole run.

L-certificates-enable-autonomy.statement: Luthier's mechanical certificates and file-held state let the AI work sustainedly through the night and across context compaction, since a pass/fail certificate makes it prudent to run the check and continue.

L-certification-forced-interpreter-rules.statement: Certifying real code forced several interpreter rules written into the spec (laws not quantified over unmentioned parameters, infinite-domain generators, tuple patterns, empty-matrix shape, lazy tables).

L-certification-impl-broken.statement: The certification machinery does not do what spec 05 promises (failing certs, stale ones, generators ignoring refinements, what runs not what was certified) and should be fixed before the next library rewrite.

L-certification-is-pointwise.statement: What is certified is not a name but a pointwise application of it on values (a chain of functions), so there are grades: point, sampled, exhaustive, proven, a chain at its weakest link.

L-certification-performance-fixes.statement: Verifying each generated value used the slow substitution evaluator; Bool predicates are now decided on the fast machine and a law's type inferred once per type.

L-certify-full-design-fisher.statement: The density-pair laws are certified over the full design (all pairs of the seven nodes) rather than over sampled graphs, because they need a non-singular Fisher information that the session-A graph does not provide.

L-certify-reloads-per-name.statement: Certification is slow because the script reloads and rechecks everything once per name; running all obligations of a file in one invocation would fix it.

L-certifying-algorithm-witness.statement: A certifying algorithm returns its result plus a witness a simple checker verifies, the refined value being the special case where the witness is the value itself, giving in general a dependent pair with a law.

L-certs-internal-not-empirical.statement: Nothing is applied to the real data; the certificates speak of internal coherence, not of whether the model describes the measurements.

L-certs-on-holes-never-match.statement: Certificates depending on holes never match because the hash is compared at import before the parent fills the holes but was computed after.

L-chain-interpretable-steps.statement: The AI generates so much output that the only workable way to use it is to chain steps whose result you can interpret.

L-check-bool-primary-derived.statement: A check is written once as a Bool (the law, composing by and/or/not) with refinement by branch as the rule, and the refined type and other presentations are derived.

L-check-exit-zero-unproven.statement: luthier check exits with code 0 even when laws are unproven, so a Stop hook would not catch the uncovered obligations.

L-check-infer-bidirectional.statement: check traverses the definitions verifying each type is a type and each body has its declared type, infer computes the type by recursion over Term, and real verifiers are bidirectional, which is where refl types or not.

L-check-refines-value-type.statement: A check done on a value refines its type (inside if p x, x has the refined type) so nobody checks it again, with the result's granularity chosen by the cost of redoing it; this applies to run results, which are checked once into the run record.

L-check-value-vs-function.statement: Checking a value is an exact computation and checking a function is sampling, but both are the same construct operation differing only in whether the check is exact or statistical.

L-check-vs-test-stages.statement: check only verifies types and registers which laws remain pending; test runs the laws, writes the certificate and marks definitions certified, reverting them to stale when a definition or a dependency changes.

L-checker-loses-laws-in-branches.statement: When the expected type has laws the checker does not inspect each branch of an if or match; it infers the type of the whole, loses the laws and raises one obligation over the whole expression.

L-checker-richer-presentation.statement: The checker may keep its richer presentation for speed, like Lean's kernel/elaborator split, provided its Term-to-core translation is written.

L-class-carries-structure.statement: A class should generate and carry its structure and give access to its records, rather than being a bare simple structure.
